_comment: What Foreman does, in the order it happens to a real enquiry. Each step maps to money the trade is currently losing — that is the point of the ordering. `art` picks the line drawing from lib/illustrations.mjs.
problemHeading: You are not losing work on price. You are losing it on silence.
problemLede: A customer rings three firms on a Tuesday lunchtime. One answers. That one usually gets the job, and it is rarely about being cheapest. The rest of the leak is quotes that went out and were never chased.

problems.label: of customers buy from whoever replies first
problems.note: Not whoever is cheapest, and not whoever is best. Whoever is first.

problems.label: calls to a working trade go unanswered
problems.note: Because you are under a floor, up a ladder, or driving.

problems.label: the average AC or boiler job you lose by not calling back
problems.note: One a month is a salary's worth of work a year.

_statsComment: These are industry-shaped figures used as framing, not measured claims about Foreman. Either source them properly before launch or soften them to 'most' and 'often' — an unsourced percentage on a B2B page is the first thing a sceptical buyer challenges.
doesLede: Six jobs, in the order they happen. Each one is a place work currently leaks out.

capabilities.title: Answers in under a minute, day or night
capabilities.body: Missed call turns into a text before they have dialled the next firm. Web form, WhatsApp and email get a real reply, not an autoresponder. Saturday night and bank holidays included.
detail: Missed-call-to-text in under 60 seconds
Web, WhatsApp, email and Facebook in one place
Out-of-hours and holiday cover
Answers in your voice, not corporate filler

capabilities.title: Asks what you would have asked
capabilities.body: Make and age of the boiler. Which rooms, how big, what floor. Access, parking, whether they own the place. By the time you read it, you know whether it is worth the drive.
detail: Question sets per trade, edited by you
Flags the time-wasters before you quote
Postcode checked against your patch
Photos requested and attached to the job

capabilities.title: Builds the quote from your price book
capabilities.body: Your rates, your margins, your terms, your letterhead. Out the same day instead of next Sunday night. Anything it is not sure about, it hands to you rather than guessing.
detail: Itemised and branded, as a link or a PDF
Your prices — it never invents one or discounts to win
Hands over when the job is unusual
You approve before it sends, until you turn that off

capabilities.title: Chases until you get an answer
capabilities.body: This is where most of the money is. Three polite follow-ups over a fortnight, stopping the moment they reply. Nobody does this by hand on a Friday at seven.
detail: Stops instantly on any reply
Asks the question that unsticks it: too dear, bad timing, or gone elsewhere?
Tells you why you lost, so the next quote is better
Reheats old quotes when the season turns

capabilities.title: Puts the survey in your diary
capabilities.body: Offers slots you actually have free, confirms, reminds the day before. The no-show rate on surveys halves when somebody gets a reminder.
detail: Reads your existing calendar
Travel time between jobs built in
Reminders by text the day before
Reschedules without you touching it

capabilities.title: Shows you where the work goes
capabilities.body: Enquiries in, quotes out, jobs won, and what each source is actually worth. Most trades are spending on something that has never produced a job.
detail: Win rate by source and by job type
What your average quote is worth
Which follow-up turned into money
One page, monthly, in plain English

approvalHeading: It does not talk to your customers behind your back
approvalBody: Every message Foreman writes goes to you first. You read it, you tap approve, it sends. That stays on for as long as you want it — some people leave it on forever, most switch it off for the routine stuff after a fortnight and keep it on for quotes over a certain value. It is your name on the van.
integrationsHeading: Sits alongside what you already use
integrationsBody: Foreman is a sales desk, not another job-management system. If you run Tradify, Jobber, ServiceM8, Commusoft or a diary and a notebook, it works with that rather than replacing it.
_integrationsComment: Do not list named integrations as available until they are actually built and tested. Naming a system you have not integrated with is the quickest way to lose a demo.
